Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in connection with C.T. Case No.83 of 2023 pending on the file of learned Addl. Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge, Phulbani, Kandhamal arising out of Phiringia P.S.
Case No.86 of 2023 for commission of offence alleged under Sections 20(b)(ii)(c) of the NDPS Act.

entities.text: Addl. Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge, Phulbani, Kandhamal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel, on instruction, submits that except the present BLAPL, no other bail application of the Petitioner relating to the aforementioned P.S. case is pending in any other Court.

4. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) by the learned Addl.
Sessions Judge, Phulbani by order dated 04.07.2024 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.
5. This is the fifth journey of the Petitioner to this Court.

Earlier bail application of the Petitioner i.e.
BLAPL No.8726 of 2023 was rejected by this Court by order dated 29.08.2023 since the same was during the currency of investigation.
Thereafter, Petitioner had moved this Court in BLAPL No.13625 of 2023.
This Court by order dated 22.02.2024 in BLAPL No.13625 of 2023 was directed him to be released on bail subject to verification of criminal antecedent.

sentences.text: 1 6 . Since it came to the fore that the Petitioner has criminal antecedents, learned Court in seisin rejected his bail application.
7. Thereafter, the Petitioner had moved this Court in BLAPL Nos.2899 of 2024 and 6101 of 2024 which were disposed of as withdrawn by orders dated 26.04.2024 and 28.06.2024 respectively.
Hence the present bail application.

8. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner is in custody since 27.05.2023 on the allegation of being involved in transportation of contraband (ganja) to the tune of 65 kgs along with co-accused.

9. Learned counsel for the Petitioner relies on the order dated 15.02.2024 passed by this Court in respect of release of the co-accused in BLAPL Nos.13491 of 2023 and 13574 of 2023 and seeks release inter alia on the ground of parity as well as delay in progress of trial.
10. Per contra, learned counsel for the State referring to the order of rejection, submits that the Petitioner have five criminal antecedents.

C)
Toshan P.S. case No.202 dt. 19.04.2022 for the offence U/s.376(1)/506 R/w Section 4 of POCSO Act

. 
D) Toshan P.S. case No.249 dt. 07.05.2022 U/s.195-A/506/509 IPC.

E) Sadar Bhiwani P.S. case No.382 dt.
23.06.2022 U/s.25/54 of Arms Act."
12. Taking note of the same and keeping in view the rigors of Section 37(1)(b)(ii) of the NDPS Act as has been rightly adverted to by the learned Public Prosecutor, this Court is not persuaded to direct the release of the Petitioner and so far as parity is concerned, the same cannot be applied mechanically.
Hence, this Court is not inclined to entertain the bail application of the Petitioner at this stage.
13. It is also stated at the Bar that in the meanwhile, six witnesses have already been examined.
14. Taking note of the same, this Court calls upon the learned Court in seisin to conclude the trial at an early date.

sentences.text: 15. Learned counsel for the State is called upon to impart necessary instructions to ensure that the prosecution witnesses are produced on the date fixed so that trial can be concluded expeditiously.
16. Copy of this order be made over the learned counsel for the State.
17. Registry is requested to communicate this order.
18. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
